# skill

AI Agent Skill Search and Management

Manage [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) (SKILL.md files) across multiple AI coding agents — Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, and more.

## Install

```default
pip install skill
```

## Quick Start

<!-- wads-docs: skip placeholder path /path/to/skill-dir -->
```python
from skill import search, create, install, validate

# Create a skill locally
skill = create("my-skill", description="My custom coding rules")

# Validate it
issues = validate("/path/to/skill-dir")

# Search for skills
results = search("react best practices", local_only=True)

# Install to an agent target
install("_local/my-skill", agent_targets=["claude-code"], scope="project")
# built-in targets: claude-code, codex, cursor, copilot, gemini, cline, windsurf (all link the SKILL.md folder;
# codex, cursor, copilot, gemini and cline share <project>/.agents/skills, so one install serves them all)
# rules-file translations, if you want them: cursor-rules, copilot-instructions, windsurf-rules, cline-rules, gemini-md
```

### Link skills from a project

If a project ships skills (in `.claude/skills/`, `{pkg}/data/skills/`, or a
dedicated folder), you can symlink them all into your agent’s skills directory
in one shot:

<!-- wads-docs: skip placeholder path /path/to/my-project -->
```python
from skill import link_skills

# Point at a project root — it finds the skills automatically
link_skills("/path/to/my-project")

# Or point at the skills folder directly
link_skills("/path/to/my-project/my_pkg/data/skills")

# Symlink into a specific target instead of ~/.claude/skills
link_skills("/path/to/my-project", target="/other/project/.claude/skills")
```

Each skill is validated before linking — invalid skills are skipped with a
warning. The target directory is also checked to ensure it’s a recognized
skills directory.

### CLI

```default
skill create my-skill --description "My custom coding rules"
skill search "react best practices" --local-only
skill validate ./my-skill/
skill list-skills
skill install _local/my-skill --agent-targets claude-code
skill install-from-package some-distribution --scope global   # the skills an installed package ships
skill gh-install owner/repo skill-name --scope user            # a GitHub-published skill, via `gh skill`
skill link-skills /path/to/project
skill link-skills /path/to/project --target ~/.claude/skills --force
skill check-wheel-skills dist/my_pkg-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl     # skills/ shipped once, as my_pkg/_skills
```

To ship a package’s top-level `skills/` inside its wheel too (the `wheel-included-skills` method), add `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]` with `"skills" = "my_pkg/_skills"` to `pyproject.toml` and check each build with `skill check-wheel-skills`. Users then run `skill install-from-package my-pkg`.

### Shell completion

Enable tab completion for all `skill` commands:

```bash
skill install-completion
```

This detects your shell (bash/zsh) and adds the registration line to your
shell config (`~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`). Restart your shell or `source` the
config file to activate.

If you prefer to set it up manually:

```bash
# Add to your shell config:
eval "$(register-python-argcomplete skill)"
```

The first time you run any `skill` command without completion set up, you’ll
see a one-time hint reminding you to run `skill install-completion`.

## Skills

This package ships agent skills you can install into any agent host with
[`gh skill`](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_skill) (don’t have it?
[install gh](https://cli.github.com/)):

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/skill skill-package-setup --agent claude-code
gh skill install thorwhalen/skill skill-build
gh skill install thorwhalen/skill skill-enable
gh skill install thorwhalen/skill skill-docs
gh skill install thorwhalen/skill skill-manage
gh skill install thorwhalen/skill skill-sync
```

| Skill                 | Use it when…                                                                               |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `skill-manage`        | searching, listing, inspecting, or installing/uninstalling skills across agents            |
| `skill-enable`        | shipping a package’s skills via `pip install` and deciding which to ship                   |
| `skill-package-setup` | deciding where a package’s skills live and making them `gh skill`-installable (maintainer) |
| `skill-build`         | authoring skills for a package by analyzing its code, tests, and docs (developer)          |
| `skill-docs`          | documenting a project’s skills in its README (developer)                                   |
| `skill-sync`          | keeping skills in sync with the source code they document (developer)                      |

These are dev/maintainer skills, so they’re not bundled in the wheel — install
them with `gh skill` as above. See `skill-package-setup` for the layout policy
this repo follows (real files in `skills/`, relative symlinks in `.claude/skills/`).

Packages can also install their own GitHub-published skills programmatically via
[`skill.install_from_github(repo, names, agent='claude-code', pin=None)`](),
a thin wrapper over the `gh skill` CLI (GitHub CLI 2.90 or later). Pass `pin='v1.2.0'` (a tag or a commit SHA) for a reproducible install that `gh skill update` leaves alone.

`skill` does not try to be an installer for every host: `gh skill` and [`npx skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) cover dozens of hosts, with pinning and lockfiles. What they do not do is check a skill: `npx skills add` installs a skill whose `name` is invalid. Run `skill validate` before either.

## Plugin System

`skill` has a registry-based plugin architecture with four extension points:

| Registry          | What it holds                        | Import                                    |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| **Agent targets** | Where agents expect skills installed | `from skill.install import agent_targets` |
| **Translators**   | SKILL.md → target format converters  | `from skill.translate import translators` |
| **Backends**      | Remote skill sources for search      | `from skill.search import backends`       |
| **Validators**    | Pluggable validation rules           | `from skill.create import validators`     |

Register at runtime:

```python
from skill.install import agent_targets, AgentTarget

agent_targets.register(
    "my-host",
    AgentTarget(
        name="my-host",
        global_path="{home}/.my-host/skills/{name}",
        project_path="{project}/.my-host/skills/{name}",
        format="skill.md",
    ),
)
```

Or via entry points in your `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project.entry-points."skill.agent_targets"]
my-host = "my_package:my_host_target"
```

See [Plugin System Documentation]() for full details on contracts, interfaces, and built-in registrations.

# skill.ai

Optional AI facade for semantic search and LLM-powered features.

All imports are lazy. This module works without any AI dependencies —
it gracefully degrades when providers are not installed.

### Functions

| [`chat`](_autosummary/skill.ai.html.md#skill.ai.chat)(prompt, \*[, system, model, temperature])   | Send a chat completion request to the configured AI provider.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`is_ai_available`](_autosummary/skill.ai.html.md#skill.ai.is_ai_available)()                                | Check if an AI provider is available.                           |

### skill.ai.chat(prompt, , system=None, model=None, temperature=0.0)

Send a chat completion request to the configured AI provider.

Provider resolution order: aisuite -> anthropic -> openai.

Raises ImportError with actionable install instructions if no
provider is available.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### skill.ai.is_ai_available()

Check if an AI provider is available.

Returns True if any supported provider can be imported and
an API key is configured (or detectable from environment).

```pycon
>>> isinstance(is_ai_available(), bool)
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

# skill.backends

Backend protocols and local filesystem backend.

### Classes

### *class* skill.backends.LocalDirSource(root)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

SkillSource backed by an arbitrary local directory of skills.

Useful for testing and for local skill packages (e.g. a git checkout).
The directory should contain `owner/name/SKILL.md` structure.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> from skill.base import Skill, SkillMeta
>>> d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> (d / 'alice' / 'greet').mkdir(parents=True)
>>> Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='greet', description='Say hi'), body='Hi!').write_to(d / 'alice' / 'greet')
>>> src = LocalDirSource(d)
>>> src.name
'local'
>>> 'alice/greet' in src
True
>>> src['alice/greet'].meta.name
'greet'
```

#### search(query, , max_results=10)

Keyword search over skill names and descriptions.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> from skill.base import Skill, SkillMeta
>>> d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> (d / 'bob' / 'python-lint').mkdir(parents=True)
>>> Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='python-lint', description='Lint Python code'), body='...').write_to(d / 'bob' / 'python-lint')
>>> src = LocalDirSource(d)
>>> results = src.search('python')
>>> len(results) > 0
True
>>> results[0].name
'python-lint'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`SkillInfo`](_autosummary/skill.base.html.md#skill.base.SkillInfo)]

### *class* skill.backends.SkillSource(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Read-only source of skills (e.g., GitHub, local directory).

`__iter__` and `__len__` are deliberately omitted — remote sources
may not support enumeration.

|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`parse_frontmatter`](_autosummary/skill.base.html.md#skill.base.parse_frontmatter)(content)  | Parse YAML frontmatter delimited by `---` from markdown content.                        |
| [`parse_skill_md`](_autosummary/skill.base.html.md#skill.base.parse_skill_md)(content)     | Parse a SKILL.md string into (SkillMeta, body).                                         |

### Classes

| [`Skill`](_autosummary/skill.base.html.md#skill.base.Skill)(meta, body[, resources, source_path])      | A fully parsed skill: frontmatter + body + resource manifest.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|

### skill.base.KNOWN_FRONTMATTER_KEYS *= frozenset({'allowed-tools', 'audience', 'compatibility', 'description', 'license', 'metadata', 'name'})*

Top-level frontmatter keys `SkillMeta` models as named fields. Anything else
is an unknown/namespaced key (e.g. another tool’s `coact:` block) and is kept
verbatim in [`SkillMeta.extra`](_autosummary/skill.base.html.md#skill.base.SkillMeta.extra) so it survives a parse→render round-trip.

### *class* skill.base.Skill(meta, body, resources=dict(), source_path=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A fully parsed skill: frontmatter + body + resource manifest.

```pycon
>>> s = Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='test', description='A test'), body='# Hello')
>>> s.meta.name
'test'
```

#### *classmethod* from_path(path)

Load a Skill from a directory containing SKILL.md.

`path` should be the skill directory (containing SKILL.md).

* **Return type:**
  [`Skill`](_autosummary/skill.base.html.md#skill.base.Skill)

#### *classmethod* from_string(content)

Parse a Skill from a SKILL.md string (no resource discovery).

```pycon
>>> s = Skill.from_string("---\nname: x\ndescription: y\n---\nbody")
>>> s.meta.name
'x'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Skill`](_autosummary/skill.base.html.md#skill.base.Skill)

#### to_string()

Render this skill as a SKILL.md string.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### write_to(path)

Write this skill to a directory, creating SKILL.md and resource dirs.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### *class* skill.base.SkillInfo(canonical_key, name, description, source, url=None, owner=None, installed=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Lightweight metadata for search results (no body).

```pycon
>>> si = SkillInfo(canonical_key='owner/test', name='test', description='A test', source='local')
>>> si.canonical_key
'owner/test'
```

### *class* skill.base.SkillMeta(name, description, audience=None, license=None, compatibility=None, metadata=dict(), allowed_tools=list(), extra=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Parsed YAML frontmatter from a SKILL.md file.

```pycon
>>> m = SkillMeta(name='test', description='A test skill')
>>> m.name
'test'
```

Unknown/namespaced top-level keys are preserved in [`extra`](_autosummary/skill.base.html.md#skill.base.SkillMeta.extra) and re-emitted
on render, so a tool’s additive frontmatter block isn’t silently dropped:

```pycon
>>> m = SkillMeta(name='t', description='d', extra={'coact': {'model': 'sonnet'}})
>>> m.to_dict()['coact']
{'model': 'sonnet'}
```

#### extra *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]*

Unknown/namespaced top-level frontmatter keys, kept verbatim for round-trip.

#### to_dict()

Convert to a dict suitable for YAML frontmatter, omitting None values.

Named fields render first (stable order); preserved [`extra`](_autosummary/skill.base.html.md#skill.base.SkillMeta.extra) keys
follow, so namespaced blocks survive `parse_skill_md` → `render_skill_md`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### skill.base.discover_resources(path)

Scan a skill directory for bundled resource subdirectories.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     p = Path(d)
...     (p / 'scripts').mkdir()
...     (p / 'scripts' / 'run.py').touch()
...     r = discover_resources(p)
...     r['scripts']
['run.py']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### skill.base.parse_frontmatter(content)

Parse YAML frontmatter delimited by `---` from markdown content.

```pycon
>>> meta, body = parse_frontmatter("---\nname: test\ndescription: A test\n---\n# Hello")
>>> meta['name']
'test'
>>> body.strip()
'# Hello'
>>> parse_frontmatter("no frontmatter here")
({}, 'no frontmatter here')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

Parse a SKILL.md string into (SkillMeta, body).

```pycon
>>> meta, body = parse_skill_md("---\nname: foo\ndescription: bar\n---\nHello")
>>> meta.name

```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`SkillMeta`](_autosummary/skill.base.html.md#skill.base.SkillMeta), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### skill.base.render_skill_md(meta, body)

Render a SKILL.md string from meta and body.

```pycon
>>> s = render_skill_md(SkillMeta(name='x', description='y'), 'Hello')
>>> 'name: x' in s and 'Hello' in s
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### skill.base.split_frontmatter(content)

`(yaml_text, body)` of markdown that opens with a `---` frontmatter block,
else `None`. The closing `---` must be a line of its own, so a value holding
`---` does not end the block (addaix/skill#35).

```pycon
>>> split_frontmatter("---\ndescription: a --- b\nname: x\n---\nbody")
('description: a --- b\nname: x\n', 'body')
>>> split_frontmatter("no frontmatter") is None
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/skill.bundled.html.md

# skill.bundled

Link a package’s bundled skills and agents into one or more Claude homes.

Packages that ship `<pkg>/data/skills/<name>/` (and `<pkg>/data/agents/<name>.md`)
all need the same ~25 lines: link each into `~/.claude/skills` (or several Claude
homes, e.g. a second account’s `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), idempotently, reporting `ok` /
`install` / `conflict` per asset and never overwriting something that is not ours
without `force`. This is that mechanism, once.

**Pure standard library and self-contained on purpose**: a package that keeps zero
runtime dependencies can copy this file instead of depending on `skill`.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, pathlib
>>> root = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> (root / "data/skills/demo").mkdir(parents=True)
>>> _ = (root / "data/skills/demo/SKILL.md").write_text("---\nname: demo\n---\n")
>>> home = root / "home"
>>> [r["action"] for r in install_bundled(root / "data", homes=[home])]
['install']
>>> [r["action"] for r in install_bundled(root / "data", homes=[home])]
['ok']
```

### Functions

| [`claude_homes`](_autosummary/skill.bundled.html.md#skill.bundled.claude_homes)()                                | Every Claude Code home on this machine: `~/.claude` and `~/.claude-*`.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`install_bundled`](_autosummary/skill.bundled.html.md#skill.bundled.install_bundled)(source_dir, \*[, homes, ...]) | Install a package's bundled skills and agents into each Claude home.     |

### skill.bundled.claude_homes()

Every Claude Code home on this machine: `~/.claude` and `~/.claude-*`.

`~/.claude` counts whenever it exists (a fresh home has no `skills` folder yet,
addaix/skill#37); another `~/.claude-*` folder counts when it has a `skills`
folder. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, when set, is included even if it has none yet.

```pycon
>>> all(isinstance(h, Path) for h in claude_homes())
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)]

### skill.bundled.install_bundled(source_dir, , homes=None, force=False, dry_run=False)

Install a package’s bundled skills and agents into each Claude home.

`source_dir` holds `skills/<name>/` directories and/or `agents/<name>.md` files
(a package’s `data` folder). `homes` defaults to [`claude_homes()`](_autosummary/skill.bundled.html.md#skill.bundled.claude_homes). Returns one
row per (home, asset): `{"home", "name", "action"}` with `action` one of

- `"ok"`: already installed (a link to the source, or an identical copy);
- `"install"`: installed now (or would be, under `dry_run`); a `"method"` key
  says `symlink` or `copy`;
- `"conflict"`: something else is at that name; left alone unless `force`.

```pycon
>>> install_bundled("/no/such/folder", homes=["/tmp/never-used"])
[]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

# _autosummary/skill.html.md

# skill

AI Agent Skill Search and Management.

Simple usage:

```default
from skill import search, install, create, list_skills, validate

# Search for skills
results = search('react best practices', local_only=True)

# Create a new skill locally
skill = create('my-skill', description='My custom skill')

# Validate a skill
issues = validate('/path/to/skill-dir')
```

Plugin registries:

```default
from skill.install import agent_targets
from skill.translate import translators
from skill.search import backends
from skill.create import validators
```

# _autosummary/skill.profiles.html.md

# skill.profiles

Per-host validation profiles for SKILL.md, and a YAML-safety check.

The open spec’s limits (what `skill.validate()` always checks) are not what
every host enforces. A skill can pass them and still be rejected or truncated by
the host it is shipped to. A [`Profile`](_autosummary/skill.profiles.html.md#skill.profiles.Profile) is data: the frontmatter keys a
host accepts and its description cap. `validate(path, profile='portable')`
adds the checks of that profile on top of the registered validators.

```pycon
>>> sorted(PROFILES)
['claude-code', 'portable', 'spec']
>>> PROFILES['portable'].max_description
200
```

### Module Attributes

| [`SPEC_KEYS`](_autosummary/skill.profiles.html.md#skill.profiles.SPEC_KEYS)   | Frontmatter keys of the open agent-skills specification.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`check_profile`](_autosummary/skill.profiles.html.md#skill.profiles.check_profile)(\*, keys, description, profile)   | Issues a host profile finds in a skill's top-level `keys` and `description`.                         |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check_yaml_safety`](_autosummary/skill.profiles.html.md#skill.profiles.check_yaml_safety)(frontmatter)                  | Flag unquoted top-level values that YAML reads differently from what was meant.                      |
| [`get_profile`](_autosummary/skill.profiles.html.md#skill.profiles.get_profile)(profile)                            | Resolve a profile name (or pass a [`Profile`](_autosummary/skill.profiles.html.md#skill.profiles.Profile) through). |

### Classes

| [`Profile`](_autosummary/skill.profiles.html.md#skill.profiles.Profile)(name[, allowed_keys, max_description])   | What one host enforces on SKILL.md frontmatter.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|

### *class* skill.profiles.Profile(name, allowed_keys=None, max_description=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What one host enforces on SKILL.md frontmatter.

`allowed_keys=None` means the host does not restrict top-level keys.
`max_description=None` means no cap beyond the open spec’s 1024.

### skill.profiles.SPEC_KEYS *= frozenset({'allowed-tools', 'compatibility', 'description', 'license', 'metadata', 'name'})*

Frontmatter keys of the open agent-skills specification.

### skill.profiles.check_profile(, keys, description, profile)

Issues a host profile finds in a skill’s top-level `keys` and `description`.

```pycon
>>> check_profile(keys=['name', 'description', 'model'], description='x' * 201,
...               profile='portable')
['Description exceeds 200 characters for profile portable (201)', "Key 'model' is not accepted by profile portable"]
>>> check_profile(keys=['name'], description='ok', profile='spec')
[]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### skill.profiles.check_yaml_safety(frontmatter)

Flag unquoted top-level values that YAML reads differently from what was meant.

A value holding `": "` is read as a new key; one holding `" #"` as a comment
(everything after it is dropped). Quoted values and block scalars are safe.

```pycon
>>> check_yaml_safety('name: x\ndescription: Use when: the user asks')
["description: unquoted value contains ': ' (YAML reads a new key); quote it"]
>>> check_yaml_safety('name: x\ndescription: Fix issue#12 now')
[]
>>> check_yaml_safety('description: Fix this #12')
["description: unquoted value contains ' #' (YAML reads a comment); quote it"]
>>> check_yaml_safety('description: "Use when: fine #1"\nname: x')
[]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### skill.profiles.get_profile(profile)

Resolve a profile name (or pass a [`Profile`](_autosummary/skill.profiles.html.md#skill.profiles.Profile) through).

```pycon
>>> get_profile('spec').name
'spec'
>>> get_profile('nope')
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
ValueError: Unknown profile 'nope'; known: claude-code, portable, spec
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Profile`](_autosummary/skill.profiles.html.md#skill.profiles.Profile)

### skill.translate.from_mdc(content)

Import a Cursor `.mdc` file as a Skill.

```pycon
>>> content = "---\ndescription: Do things\nglobs: '*.py'\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n# Rules"
>>> s = from_mdc(content)
>>> s.meta.description
'Do things'
>>> s.meta.metadata.get('cursor.globs')
'*.py'
```

Globs as Cursor itself writes them (unquoted, not valid YAML) are kept verbatim:

```pycon
>>> from_mdc("---\nglobs: **/*.py, **/*.ts\n---\nx").meta.metadata['cursor.globs']
'**/*.py, **/*.ts'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Skill`](_autosummary/skill.base.html.md#skill.base.Skill)

### skill.translate.lost_fields(skill, , target_format)

What translating *skill* to *target_format* drops; `[]` for a lossless format.

```pycon
>>> from skill.base import SkillMeta
>>> s = Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='t', description='d', license='MIT'), body='x')
>>> lost_fields(s, target_format='mdc')
['license']
>>> lost_fields(s, target_format='skill.md')
[]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### skill.translate.to_cline_rule(skill)

Translate a Skill to a Cline rule file (Markdown; always active).

`metadata` key `cline.paths` becomes the `paths` frontmatter that makes the
rule conditional. Lossy: no progressive disclosure, and `allowed-tools`,
`license` and bundled resources are dropped.

```pycon
>>> from skill.base import SkillMeta
>>> s = Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='lint', description='Lint rules'), body='Use ruff.')
>>> to_cline_rule(s).splitlines()[:3]
['# lint', '', '> Lint rules']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### skill.translate.to_copilot_instructions(skill)

Translate a Skill to GitHub Copilot instructions format.

Produces a Markdown section suitable for appending to
`.github/copilot-instructions.md`. Lossy: no frontmatter support
beyond `applyTo`, no progressive disclosure, no resources.

```pycon
>>> from skill.base import SkillMeta
>>> s = Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='lint', description='Lint rules'), body='Use ruff.')
>>> md = to_copilot_instructions(s)
>>> '## lint' in md
True
>>> 'Use ruff.' in md
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### skill.translate.to_gemini_md(skill)

Translate a Skill to a section of Gemini CLI’s `GEMINI.md`.

Lossy: the file is always loaded (no progressive disclosure), and
`allowed-tools`, `license` and bundled resources are dropped.

```pycon
>>> from skill.base import SkillMeta
>>> s = Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='lint', description='Lint rules'), body='Use ruff.')
>>> to_gemini_md(s).splitlines()[0]
'## lint'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### skill.translate.to_mdc(skill)

Translate a Skill to Cursor `.mdc` format.

Lossy: `allowed-tools`, `license`, bundled resources, and progressive
disclosure semantics are lost.

```pycon
>>> from skill.base import SkillMeta
>>> s = Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='test', description='Test skill'), body='Do stuff.')
>>> mdc = to_mdc(s)
>>> 'description: Test skill' in mdc
True
>>> 'Do stuff.' in mdc
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### skill.translate.to_windsurf_rule(skill)

Translate a Skill to a Windsurf rule, applied when the model judges it relevant.

`metadata` keys `windsurf.trigger` (default `model_decision`) and
`windsurf.globs` pass through. Lossy: `allowed-tools`, `license` and
bundled resources are dropped.

```pycon
>>> from skill.base import SkillMeta
>>> s = Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='lint', description='Lint rules'), body='Use ruff.')
>>> print(to_windsurf_rule(s))
---
trigger: model_decision
description: Lint rules
---

Use ruff.
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### skill.translate.translate(skill, , target_format)

Translate a Skill to the specified target format.

```pycon
>>> from skill.base import SkillMeta
>>> s = Skill(meta=SkillMeta(name='x', description='y'), body='z')
>>> 'alwaysApply' in translate(s, target_format='mdc')
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

# _autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md

# skill.wheel

The `wheel-included-skills` placement method: a tested build recipe.

The real skill files live once, in the repository’s top-level `skills/<name>/` (where
`gh skill` and the wider ecosystem look), and the build copies that folder into the
wheel as `<pkg>/_skills/` so a `pip install` carries them too (addaix/skill#8, #31).
The copy exists only in the built wheel, never in the repository, so `gh skill` sees
each skill once; it is a copy, never a symlink, because whether `gh skill` follows a
symlink is unverified.

- [`wheel_skills_config()`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.wheel_skills_config) gives the `pyproject.toml` settings as a dict (hatchling
  or setuptools), to merge into an existing file; [`wheel_skills_snippet()`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.wheel_skills_snippet) the same
  as TOML text, for a file that has no such table yet.
- [`check_wheel_skills()`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.check_wheel_skills) checks a built wheel against the repository: every
  `skills/<name>/` file is in the wheel under `<pkg>/_skills/<name>/`, byte for byte,
  every `SKILL.md` exactly once, and the repository holds each skill once.
- `skill install-from-package <distribution>` then finds `<pkg>/_skills` in the
  installed package (`skill.install.PACKAGE_SKILLS_SUBPATHS`).

```pycon
>>> print(wheel_skills_snippet("my_pkg"))
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"skills" = "my_pkg/_skills"
```

### Module Attributes

| [`WHEEL_SKILLS_DIR`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.WHEEL_SKILLS_DIR)   | The folder, inside the import package, that the build copies `skills/` to.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`wheel_skills_config`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.wheel_skills_config)(package, \*[, backend, ...])   | The `pyproject.toml` settings that put `source` into the wheel as `<package>/<target_dir>`, as a nested dict to merge into the file (with tomlkit, say) rather than append to it.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`wheel_skills_snippet`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.wheel_skills_snippet)(package, \*[, backend, ...])  | [`wheel_skills_config()`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.wheel_skills_config) as `pyproject.toml` text, for a file that has none of these tables yet (merge the dict instead when it has). |
| [`check_wheel_skills`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.check_wheel_skills)(wheel[, repo_root, ...])        | Check a built wheel against the repository it was built from.                                                                                                                       |

### Classes

| [`WheelSkillsReport`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.WheelSkillsReport)([skills, problems, warnings])   | What [`check_wheel_skills()`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.check_wheel_skills) found.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### skill.wheel.WHEEL_SKILLS_DIR *= '_skills'*

The folder, inside the import package, that the build copies `skills/` to.

### *class* skill.wheel.WheelSkillsReport(skills=list(), problems=list(), warnings=list())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What [`check_wheel_skills()`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.check_wheel_skills) found. `ok` when there are no `problems`;
`warnings` (such as a developer skill shipped to users) do not fail it.

### skill.wheel.check_wheel_skills(wheel, repo_root='.', , package=None, source='skills', target_dir='_skills')

Check a built wheel against the repository it was built from.

Problems (`report.ok` is false):

- a repository skill (`<source>/<name>/`) missing from the wheel, or one of its
  files missing or different in `<package>/<target_dir>/<name>/`;
- a skill whose `SKILL.md` the wheel holds more than once (anywhere), or a
  skill in the wheel’s `<target_dir>` that the repository does not have;
- a skill whose real `SKILL.md` the repository holds in more than one
  non-hidden place (`gh skill` reports duplicates), or a committed copy of the
  in-wheel folder (`<package>/<target_dir>`) in the repository.

#### WARNING
a skill whose `audience` is `developer` ships to users.

`package` defaults to the one import package that has a `<target_dir>` in the
wheel.

* **Return type:**
  [`WheelSkillsReport`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.WheelSkillsReport)

### skill.wheel.wheel_skills_config(package, , backend='hatch', source='skills', target_dir='_skills')

The `pyproject.toml` settings that put `source` into the wheel as
`<package>/<target_dir>`, as a nested dict to merge into the file (with tomlkit,
say) rather than append to it.

- `hatch`: `force-include`. hatchling copies the files, following links, and
  skips its built-in excludes (`.DS_Store`, `.pytest_cache`…).
- `setuptools`: `<package>.<target_dir>` declared as a package whose directory is
  `source`, with all its files as package data.

The build must see `source`: a wheel built from an sdist (the default of
`python -m build`) needs it in the sdist too.

```pycon
>>> wheel_skills_config("p")
{'tool': {'hatch': {'build': {'targets': {'wheel': {'force-include': {'skills': 'p/_skills'}}}}}}}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### skill.wheel.wheel_skills_snippet(package, , backend='hatch', source='skills', target_dir='_skills')

[`wheel_skills_config()`](_autosummary/skill.wheel.html.md#skill.wheel.wheel_skills_config) as `pyproject.toml` text, for a file that has none
of these tables yet (merge the dict instead when it has).

```pycon
>>> print(wheel_skills_snippet("p", backend="setuptools"))
[tool.setuptools]
packages = ["p", "p._skills"]
package-dir = { "p._skills" = "skills" }
package-data = { "p._skills" = ["**/*"] }
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`skill` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `skill-build`

Skill-building tooling for the skill package. Build AI agent skills for any Python package by analyzing its code, tests, and docs. Use this skill when the user wants to create skills for a package, analyze a codebase to suggest what skills would be useful, generate SKILL.md files from existing code/tests/docs, or when someone says things like “make skills for this package”, “what skills should this project have”, “create a skill from this module”, or “generate skills”. Also trigger when the user points at a package and asks for AI-powered interfaces to it.

```bash
gh skill install addaix/skill skill-build --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/skill-build`](https://github.com/addaix/skill/tree/HEAD/skills/skill-build).

### `skill-docs`

Skill documentation tooling for the skill package. Document a project’s AI agent skills in the README and other formats. Use this skill when the user wants to add skills documentation to a README, explain what skills a project offers, write a “Skills” section, generate skill installation instructions, or when asked things like “document the skills”, “add skills to the README”, “how should I present skills to users”, or “write skill usage examples”. Also trigger when updating a README for a package that has skills in .claude/skills/ or {pkg}/data/skills/.

```bash
gh skill install addaix/skill skill-docs --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/skill-docs`](https://github.com/addaix/skill/tree/HEAD/skills/skill-docs).

### `skill-enable`

Ship a Python package’s AI agent skills with `pip install` — and decide WHICH skills to ship. Use when the user asks how to include skills in their package distribution, make skills available after `pip install`, ship SKILL.md files with their package, set up `{pkg}/data/skills/`, configure package-data, add a skills installer/convenience function, or says “how do users get my skills after pip install”, “ship skills with my package”, “distribute skills”, “package skills”, or “enable skills in my library”. Also trigger when working on pyproject.toml and the project has skills to distribute. The overall layout decision (where real files live, the `.claude/skills/` symlink bridge, spec compliance) is owned by **skill-package-setup**; this skill covers the pip-distribution mechanics and audience classification.

```bash
gh skill install addaix/skill skill-enable --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/skill-enable`](https://github.com/addaix/skill/tree/HEAD/skills/skill-enable).

### `skill-manage`

Skill management tooling for the skill package. Search, list, inspect, and manage AI agent skills across agents and projects. Use this skill when the user wants to find skills, see what skills are installed, check where skills are linked, inspect a skill’s contents, install or uninstall skills, compare skills across agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot), or says things like “what skills do I have”, “find a skill for X”, “show me the skill”, “where are my skills”, “install this skill”, “remove that skill”, “list skills”, or “search skills”. Trigger on any skill inventory, discovery, or housekeeping request.

```bash
gh skill install addaix/skill skill-manage --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/skill-manage`](https://github.com/addaix/skill/tree/HEAD/skills/skill-manage).

### `skill-package-setup`

Canonical, agent-agnostic policy for WHERE a package’s AI agent skills live and HOW they are distributed so they’re discoverable by `gh skill` (and any agent host — Copilot, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Claude) AND, where wanted, shipped with `pip install`. Use this skill to set up skills for a new package, migrate an existing repo to the canonical layout, consolidate skills scattered across `.claude/skills/` / `skills/` / `{pkg}/data/skills/`, make every SKILL.md spec-clean, or answer “where should my package’s skills live”. Also the authority other skills defer to (e.g. wads-skillify). Triggers on “set up skills”, “where should skills live”, “make skills gh-skill installable”, “migrate/restructure the skills layout”, “skillify this repo”. Maintainer skill.

```bash
gh skill install addaix/skill skill-package-setup --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/skill-package-setup`](https://github.com/addaix/skill/tree/HEAD/skills/skill-package-setup).

### `skill-sync`

Skill maintenance tooling for the skill package. Keep AI agent skills in sync with their source package code. Use this skill when a package’s code, API, or behavior has changed and its skills may be outdated, when the user says “update the skills”, “skills are stale”, “sync skills with code”, “refresh skills”, or when you notice that skill instructions reference functions/classes/patterns that no longer exist in the codebase. Also use after major refactors, API changes, or version bumps.

```bash
gh skill install addaix/skill skill-sync --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/skill-sync`](https://github.com/addaix/skill/tree/HEAD/skills/skill-sync).

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://addaix.github.io/skill/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`skill.md`](https://addaix.github.io/skill/skill.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://addaix.github.io/skill/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
